source.title: Routing-Aware Head Amplification for Multimodal Long-Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
source.authors: Chu-Hao Zhou; Zong-Han Wu; Hao-Lang Lu; K. Wang; Wei-Ran Yao; Linsey Pang; P. Mehrotra; Qing-Song Wen; Yi Shao

record.tranche_reason: The paper cites Olsson et al. among prior work on attention-head routing, but its own measurements and interventions concern multimodal visual-evidence and previous-CoT routing, not induction-head behavior or its formation during training.
record.gate_note: The paper measures and amplifies heads attending to visual tokens or previous-CoT tokens. It does not test repeated-token copying, induction-head formation, or the timing of induction relative to in-context learning. The reported layer transitions are recorded as findings about a related but different construct.
record.test_reason: Olsson et al. is cited only among prior work on sparse head routing. The paper's measurements are of attention ratios to visual and previous-CoT tokens in multimodal models, and its intervention amplifies those heads. It does not measure induction behaviour, previous-token composition, training dynamics, or in-context learning versus token index.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that training-free, routing-aware amplification of visual heads in shallow layers and previous-CoT heads in deeper layers improves multimodal long-CoT reasoning and hallucination robustness. The reported average gain is about 4.6% across three models and seven benchmarks.
record.recipe_differences: Not a reproduction or test of induction-head methods; the paper proposes inference-time amplification of multimodal visual-routing and previous-CoT-routing heads.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported routing-transition boundary differs by model: around layer 2 for Kimi-VL and around layer 4 for Ocean-R1 and R1-Onevision.

fits_no_version.finding: Previous-CoT attention mass in three multimodal long-CoT models shows a shallow-to-deep jump: around layer 2 (Kimi-VL) and layer 4 (Ocean-R1, R1-Onevision).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multimodal long-CoT models show model-dependent depth-wise stratification of attention to their earlier reasoning tokens.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP 2026)
record.problems: The paper reports the routing transition locations in text, but gives no uncertainty estimates for them. Its routing findings concern multimodal source routing and do not directly establish induction-head behavior.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version results are reported. Main benchmark scores and intervention ablations are omitted because they evaluate the proposed multimodal hallucination-mitigation method, not induction-head behavior or the training dynamics in the claim.

untested.parts: all; no induction score in the multimodal models

record.verdict_notes: Not a test of the claim. The benchmark gains and ablations evaluate the authors' own method and are rightly left out. The 'transition' in R1–R3 is across layer depth, not across training time, so it does not bear on V2 or V7.

versions.untested_parts: Induction-head composition with previous-token heads and [A][B] … [A] → [B] copying.
Abrupt formation, training-loss bump, and timing relative to in-context learning.
Whether induction heads carry most in-context learning in large transformers.
Whether induction-behavior heads occur across model families, sizes, runs, architectures, or modalities.
Dependence of induction-head formation and in-context learning on data and training setup.
Whether few-shot task learning mainly uses mechanisms other than induction heads.
Whether induction-head formation comprises multiple sub-steps or overlapping transitions.
